decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-25493630) discusses the synergistic anti-tumor activity of EZH2 inhibitors (EPZ-6438, which is tazemetostat) in combination with CHOP in preclinical models of germinal center non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHL). The specific mutant mentioned in the evidence is EZH2 Y646F (e.g., in the WSU-DLCL2 xenograft model). The claim in question concerns the variant EZH2 Y407I in pancreas lymphoma. The evidence does not mention the Y407I variant, nor does it mention pancreas lymphoma as a specific disease context (it refers generally to germinal center NHL). Therefore, there is insufficient evidence to support, revise, or refute the specific claim regarding Y407I in pancreas lymphoma.

citations.quote: We report here that combining EPZ-6438 with CHOP in preclinical cell culture and mouse models results in dramatic synergy for cell killing in EZH2 mutant germinal center NHL cells . . . Finally, tumor growth inhibition was assessed in 3 different EZH2 mutant lymphoma xenograft models (materials and methods section 6). . . . In WSU-DLCL2 xenograft bearing mice, tumor growth inhibition (TGI) was achieved at all EPZ-6438 doses and schedules employed, and was better than CHOP alon . . . EPZ-6438/CHOP combinations show enhanced anti-tumor activity compared to single agents in several EZH2 mutant
lymphoma xenograft models. . . . WSU-DLCL2 (EZH2 Y646F) xenograft-bearing mice were treated for 28 days as indicated.
